newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares push higher before long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares push higher before long weekend.

text.p: Italian shares ended higher on Friday ahead of a long weekend with Italian markets closed on Monday for the Epiphany holiday.

The Milan bourse was pulled up by Wall Street gains, foreign buying and a robust telecommunications sector as well as a strong performance by agri-industrial group Montedison on talk before the market closed that a high percentage of its warrants had been exercised by a December 30, 1996 deadline.
Montedison announced after trading finished that 96.7 percent of 1994-1997 warrants had been exercised, with subscription provisionally totalling 1.037 trillion lire ($675 million) worth of shares.
Montedison ended up 3.21 percent at 1062 lire.
The bluechip Mib30 index ended 0.91 percent firmer at 15715 while the all-share Mibtel was 0.81 percent up at 10573.

Troubled information technology group Olivetti recovered more than two percent to 547 lire per share on renewed speculation over a possible sale of its personal computer unit, for which Olivetti is seeking a buyer.

Car maker Fiat exhausted the near term beneficial effects of a government incentive announced early this week to get people to buy more cars and boost the flagging sector. Fiat limped 1.82 percent lower on the day to 4380.
Newcomer Seat, the yellow pages phone directory group spun off from state telecommunications holding Stet last month, gained 1.46 percent to 618 lire.

On the macro economic front, at home traders are watching for progress in a long-running engineering and metalworkers' dispute with employers over pay. Formal talks are due to resume with Labour Minister Tiziano Treu next Wednesday.
Abroad, eyes are on U.S. non-farm payrolls data out next week, which are likely to dominate markets.
